power.exceptional: Forcefulness of legend — his tachiai lands like a falling tree and a single committed shove can end a bout. Opponents arrive at the shikiri already bracing for impact, knowing no amount of preparation makes the first clash safe. At this level, raw power rewrites matchmaking: stables game-plan specifically around surviving him.
power.outstanding: A genuinely powerful frame that few men at this level can withstand. When he gets his hips under an opponent, the lift is almost inevitable, and sustained belt pressure breaks grips that hold against anyone else. Coaches treat his strength as a primary weapon to be set up, not a bonus to fall back on.
power.strong: Solid, dependable strength — more than enough to move most men off their mark and punish any opponent who tries to stall the bout. He can win clinches through sheer force when technique runs even, and his forward surges are respected across the division. Not a one-punch finisher, but a reliable closer once position is secured.
power.capable: Adequate power for his rank. He won't overwhelm anyone through brute force, but he holds the center comfortably in the clinch and rarely gives ground without reason. Coaches expect his strength to meet the moment — no more, no less — and build his game plans around technique and positioning.
power.developing: Still building the deep muscle and leverage his rank demands. The raw potential is visible in training — he moves heavier loads this basho than last — but in-ring application lags behind. Opponents who recognize the gap lean on him early, hoping to close the bout before his frame finishes maturing.
power.limited: Noticeably outpowered by most opponents at this level. He compensates with footwork, timing, and angle changes, but sustained belt battles rarely end in his favor. A stalled clinch against a heavier man is essentially a losing position, and strategy reflects it.
power.struggling: Physically overmatched in nearly every contest. Opponents walk him backward almost at will, and any attempt to trade pressure head-on collapses quickly. Survival depends entirely on avoiding the clinch and manufacturing chaos before his disadvantage gets exposed.

speed.exceptional: Preternaturally quick — his first step and reaction time are genuinely hard to photograph, let alone counter. By the time opponents set their feet, he has already chosen his grip, his angle, and his finish. At this level, speed is less an attribute than a weapon that rewrites the tempo of every bout he enters.
speed.outstanding: Fast enough to regularly catch opponents flat-footed before they can establish grips or defensive posture. He turns hesitation into defeat, punishing any moment of indecision with a clean redirection or a sharp lateral step. Game plans against him center almost entirely on not getting drawn into a speed contest.
speed.strong: Quick on his feet, able to exploit fleeting openings that slower men would miss entirely. He reads momentum shifts half a beat before his peers and uses that window to steer bouts into shapes he prefers. Not elite, but consistently one of the faster men in any given matchup.
speed.capable: Moves adequately for his preferred style. His speed is neither a pronounced liability nor a weapon — it simply keeps him in step with the tempo most bouts naturally settle into. Enough to execute his game, not enough to dictate someone else's.
speed.developing: Could be quicker. His timing is still maturing, and momentary opportunities slip past him on the clay more often than a coach would like. Film sessions show the opening clearly; matching that read in real time is the work still ahead.
speed.limited: Noticeably sluggish compared to his peers. Opponents dictate the pace, choose the grip, and leave him chasing the bout rather than shaping it. Lateral adjustments in particular are a recurring problem against more mobile men.
speed.struggling: Painfully slow to react. He is easy to outmaneuver, easy to pull down, and easy to time — and faster opponents routinely land their setup before he has even committed to his tachiai. A glaring, consistent weakness at this level.

balance.exceptional: His root is the stuff of legend — veteran rikishi describe pushing him as trying to shove a mountain that pushes back. His center of gravity is an anchor that opponents seem to bend around rather than displace. Throws, pull-downs, and sudden momentum changes that would fell anyone else barely register.
balance.outstanding: Exceptionally stable under immense pressure. He rarely loses footing even in desperate, tangled scrambles, and he recovers cleanly from positions that leave other men collapsed on the clay. Coaches trust him to survive chaos that would finish most of the division.
balance.strong: Well-grounded and composed. He recovers remarkably well from disadvantaged positions and awkward angles, and sudden throws rarely land cleanly against him. A dependable foundation that lets his other tools work.
balance.capable: Adequate stability for competitive sumo. He holds steady in standard grappling situations and doesn't give up cheap losses on throws, though prolonged pressure from a stronger man will eventually tell. Nothing to exploit, nothing to lean on.
balance.developing: Sometimes caught leaning or off-angle. His stability is a work in progress and can fail under sustained heavy pressure, particularly late in long bouts when legs fade. The fundamentals are there — consistency is the next step.
balance.limited: Unsteady under real pressure. He is noticeably vulnerable to throws, pull-downs, and sudden shifts in momentum, and opposing coaches routinely script bouts around tipping him off-balance. Even a half-committed throw attempt can succeed.
balance.struggling: Falls far too easily. Fundamental stability issues severely limit what he can attempt both offensively and defensively, and any opponent with a credible throwing kimarite turns bouts against him into a formality.

technique.exceptional: A transcendent master technician. Every grip, every angle, every timing read is deliberate, precise, and executed with a fluency most wrestlers never approach. Bouts with him feel less like contests than demonstrations — the kimarite is decided long before it lands.
technique.outstanding: Highly skilled and deeply intuitive. He reads complex situations instantly and executes with the crisp clarity of a seasoned veteran, chaining setups and counters so smoothly that opponents rarely get a second chance at a bad position. Rewards study and punishes mistakes equally.
technique.strong: A genuinely good technical foundation, with reliable execution of his preferred throwing and twisting techniques. He finishes what he starts, rarely botches familiar setups, and adapts his grip intelligently when the first plan fails. A craftsman the coaches trust.
technique.capable: Sound fundamental basics. He executes his core moves cleanly when the correct opportunity presents itself, though he seldom invents solutions on the fly. Enough craft to match most peers — not enough to impose his game on unfamiliar styles.
technique.developing: His technique is improving but remains frustratingly inconsistent, particularly under heavy pressure when reps haven't yet built confidence. Clean executions in the keiko-ba still misfire in the tournament hall, and he knows it.
technique.limited: Relies almost entirely on physicality over craft. Technical sophistication is a gaping hole in his sumo game, and opponents with sharper fundamentals dismantle him the moment raw force stops working.
technique.struggling: Severely lacks the technical repertoire needed to compete effectively. His options in any given position are obvious and few, and opponents routinely exploit the predictability — even lower-ranked men find answers against him.

Defensive_Stalwart.label: Defensive Stalwart
Defensive_Stalwart.description: Calm, grounded, and almost impossible to rush. He absorbs pressure and turns it into opportunity, waiting for the moment his opponent overcommits.

Explosive_Blitzer.label: Explosive Blitzer
Explosive_Blitzer.description: The tachiai is his weapon. He ends fights in seconds — or he doesn't end them at all. Longer bouts expose a stamina cliff that opponents try desperately to reach.

Acrobatic_Trickster.label: Acrobatic Trickster
Acrobatic_Trickster.description: Slippery, inventive, and infuriating to fight. He uses unpredictable angles, impeccable timing, and clever misdirection to make heavier, stronger opponents look completely foolish.

Immovable_Mountain.label: Immovable Mountain
Immovable_Mountain.description: Once he plants himself, he is not going anywhere. His center of gravity is almost inhumanly low, and his patience is unlimited.

All_Rounder.label: All-Rounder
All_Rounder.description: No obvious weaknesses, no single predictable style. He adapts to whatever the bout demands — which is what makes him so difficult to game-plan against.

Zekkouchou.label: Zekkouchou (絶好調)
Zekkouchou.tooltip: Legs are deeply rooted; lungs are full. Maximum resistance to late-bout fatigue and throws.

Bachi-bachi.label: Bachi-bachi (ばちばち)
Bachi-bachi.tooltip: Moving with snap and vigor. Capable of sustained pushing attacks.

Iki-girashite.label: Iki-girashite (息を切らして)
Iki-girashite.tooltip: Starting to breathe heavily. Susceptible to fatigue in extended grappling (Yotsu) bouts.

Koshi-kudake.label: Koshi-kudake (腰砕け)
Koshi-kudake.tooltip: Legs are entirely gone. Highly vulnerable to pull-downs (Hikiotoshi) and slap-downs.

Shin-Gi-Tai.label: Shin-Gi-Tai (心技体)
Shin-Gi-Tai.tooltip: Mind, technique, and body are aligned. Highly resistant to Henka (sidesteps) and pressure.

Kiai juubun.label: Kiai juubun (気合十分)
Kiai juubun.tooltip: Focused and aggressive. Likely to initiate a strong, forward-moving tachiai (initial charge).

Mayoi.label: Mayoi (迷い)
Mayoi.tooltip: Second-guessing their sumo. Tachiai may lack power; prone to being pushed back early.

Fugainai.label: Fugainai (不甲斐ない)
Fugainai.tooltip: Completely demoralized. Prone to easy mistakes, false starts (Matta), and yielding the belt.

Taiki Bansei.label: Taiki Bansei (大器晩成)
Taiki Bansei.tooltip: A generational talent capable of reaching Yokozuna. Exceptional stat growth ceilings.

Soshitsu Ari.label: Soshitsu Ari (素質あり)
Soshitsu Ari.tooltip: Strong fundamentals. A definite San'yaku (champion) candidate if trained rigorously.

Mikan no Taiki.label: Mikan no Taiki (未完の大器)
Mikan no Taiki.tooltip: Average prospect. Will require specialized, intense training to survive the top division.

Genkai.label: Genkai (限界)
Genkai.tooltip: Physical limits are apparent. Best suited as a reliable lower-division stable pillar.
